title: MS-DETR: Efficient DETR Training with Mixed Supervision

problem.summary: DETR is trained with one-to-one supervision that promotes a single candidate per ground-truth object but gives no direct supervision to the candidate generation step, which slows training and yields lower-quality detection candidates than NMS-based detectors at the same budget.
statements: DETR's one-to-one training objective provides no explicit supervision for generating multiple object detection candidates.
Candidate quality in DETR depends indirectly on decoder cross-attention, making training inefficient (many epochs needed to converge).
Existing ways of adding one-to-many supervision require extra parallel decoders or extra object queries, raising computation and memory cost.

evidence.quote: The traditional training procedure using one-to-one supervision in the original DETR lacks direct supervision for the object detection candidates.
the DETR training procedure lacks explicit supervision for generating multiple object detection candidates.
Existing methods depend on the additional parallel weight-sharing decoder.

background.summary: Builds on DETR and its training-efficient variants (Deformable DETR, Conditional DETR, DAB-DETR) and on DETR variants that add one-to-many supervision through extra decoders/queries (DN-DETR, Group DETR, Hybrid DETR, DINO); the claimed gap is that none of these modify the supervision of the primary decoder itself, while DETA removes one-to-one supervision and brings NMS back.

relatedWork.name: Deformable DETR
relatedWork.relation: training-efficient baseline that replaces cross-attention with deformable attention
relatedWork.quote: Deformable DETR [48] uses deformable attention, an extension of deformable convolution [7], that selects the highly informative regions, to replace the original crossattention architecture.

relatedWork.name: Group DETR / DN-DETR
relatedWork.relation: one-to-many supervision variants that rely on additional parallel decoders
relatedWork.quote: Group DETR [4, 5] instead learns the object queries of the additional decoders.

relatedWork.name: DETA
relatedWork.relation: closest prior work doing one-to-many supervision on a single decoder, but drops one-to-one supervision and reintroduces NMS
relatedWork.quote: The mixture of one-to-one and one-to-many supervisions on the single decoder without using NMS is underexplored.

evidence.quote: Oneto-many supervision assigns one ground-truth object to multiple object queries to speed up DETR training.
The latter part is similar to NMS postprocessing, and the former part is like most detectors.

solution.summary: MS-DETR mixes one-to-one supervision with additional one-to-many supervision applied directly to the object queries of the primary (inference) decoder, using an extra box/class prediction head that is active only during training so inference is unchanged.
solution.approach: Add a one-to-many prediction head (box + class predictors) supervised with top-K matching on the primary decoder queries, optionally after reordering decoder layers to cross-attention then self-attention, with no extra decoders or queries.
components: one-to-many box and class predictors on the primary decoder
matching score combining classification score and IoU with weight alpha and threshold tau
decoder layer order cross-attention -> self-attention -> FFN
one-to-many supervision placed on internal queries output from cross-attention
shared weights between one-to-one and one-to-many predictors

evidence.quote: We propose to supervise the queries of the primary decoder with the mixture of one-to-one supervision and additional one-to-many supervision to improve the training efficiency.
MS-DETR does not introduce additional decoders, additional queries, and performs one-to-many supervision merely on the original decoder.
the additional modules only influence the training process and the inference process remains unchanged.

experiments.summary: Evaluated on COCO train2017/val2017 with ResNet-50 backbones over 12- and 24-epoch schedules on several DETR baselines, comparing against and combining with one-to-many supervision variants, plus ablations of the matching hyperparameters, supervision placement, predictor weight sharing, and an instance-segmentation transfer test.

evidence.quote: the gains over DAB-Deformable-DETR, Deformable DETR, and Deformable DETR++ are 3.7, 3.7, and 1.8 in terms of mAP under 12 epochs.
Table 7 shows that MS-DETR significantly improves the mask mAP of the baseline by 3.2 mAP under 12 epochs training schedule.
the additional time from the one-to-many supervision is minor

limitations.summary: The authors state no explicit limitations; evident ones are that gains shrink as baselines/training get stronger (+1.1 mAP over DINO at 24 epochs), the method introduces matching hyperparameters (K, tau, alpha) that must be tuned, and all results use ResNet-50 backbones on COCO.
items: Gains over the strongest baseline decrease with longer training schedules (+1.1 mAP at 24 epochs vs +2.4 at 12 epochs over DINO).
One-to-many matching depends on tuned hyperparameters K, threshold tau and score weight alpha.
Experiments are restricted to DETR-family detectors with ResNet-50 backbones on COCO.
Placing the one-to-many supervision on the wrong decoder signals (internal self-attention queries) degrades results.

evidence.quote: We empirically find that our approach achieves optimal performance when K = 6.
A large value of K causes the object imbalance problem
our improvement is also greater: +1.4 mAP vs +2.4 mAP and +0.8 mAP vs +1.1 mAP, for 12 epochs and 24 epochs, respectively.

algorithms: top-K one-to-many matching with score threshold

equations.name: MatchScore (one-to-many matching)
equations.expr: MatchScore(s, b, c̄, b̄) = α·s_c̄ + (1 − α)·IoU(b, b̄)

equations.name: one-to-many loss
equations.expr: L_1m = Σ_n Σ_i≤K_n (ℓ_c1m(s_ni, s̄_n) + ℓ_b1m(b_ni, b̄_n))

deploymentClaims: Additional one-to-many heads affect only training; inference is unchanged from the baseline DETR.
MS-DETR adds only ~2 minutes per training epoch and ~127M (~2%) GPU memory relative to the baseline, versus +28-36 minutes and +40-60% memory for Hybrid/Group DETR.

evidence.quote: the additional modules only influence the training process and the inference process remains unchanged.
our method incurs only a minor increase of 127M memory
